title: Class 9 Maths, A Whole Year: Term 1 and Term 2
subtitle: Start here. The whole Class 9 maths year on one page: Term 1 (NCERT Ganita Manjari Part I, Chapters 1 to 8) and Term 2 (Part II, Chapters 9 to 14), with the one idea in each chapter, what it needs first, and links to every chapter's step-by-step roadmap. Written for students who find maths hard, and the teachers and parents helping them.

changelog.text: Added an 'About this roadmap' step: who it is for, how it differs from the textbook, and licence.
First version: the whole year in one roadmap, organised by term, with every chapter's one idea, what it needs first, pacing and revision links.

topics.label: Start here: the year at a glance
topics.desc:
**Goal:** see the whole Class 9 maths year in one place, and know where to start.

The year has two terms. **Term 1** follows Part I of the NCERT textbook *Ganita Manjari* (Chapters 1 to 8). **Term 2** follows Part II (Chapters 9 to 14). Every chapter has its own step-by-step roadmap, written for students who find maths hard.

children.label: How to use this page
children.desc:
- **Pick your term below**, then the chapter you are on. Each box opens a short summary with a link to the chapter's own roadmap.
- **Every chapter starts with *Check yourself*.** Do it first. It points to the exact small skills to fix before the chapter.
- **Progress is saved inside each chapter's roadmap**, on this device.
- **Fallen behind?** Go back to the chapter named under *Needs first*. That is usually where the real gap is.

**One idea runs through the whole year: every chapter is built from a few ideas you already have.** Each chapter's summary below names its one idea and what it needs first.

children.label: About this roadmap
children.desc:
**What it is.** The starting page for the whole Class 9 maths year: Term 1 follows Part I of the NCERT textbook *Ganita Manjari* (Chapters 1 to 8) and Term 2 follows Part II (Chapters 9 to 14). Every chapter has its own roadmap.

**Who it is for.** Class 9 students who find maths hard, or who have fallen behind and want to catch up. It also works for revision, and for the teachers and parents helping them: the last milestone is written for adults.

**What this page does.** It lists every chapter by term, with its one idea, what it needs first, and a link to its *Check yourself*. It also links each chapter's exit ticket, for revision before exams. It does not teach the chapters itself: open a chapter to start.

**Time needed.** The lesson plans add up to 66 periods in Term 1 and 35 in Term 2.

**Can you trust it?** Every number in the worked examples and answers was checked by a computer program, and every picture was drawn specially for this roadmap. All the examples are original, so students still get fresh practice from the textbook itself. If you spot a mistake, use **Report a problem** at the top of the page.

**Not official.** This is a free, independent resource. It follows the NCERT textbook but is not made or endorsed by NCERT or CBSE. It is shared under the **CC BY-SA 4.0** licence: you may copy, adapt and share it, including in your school, as long as you credit it and share your version the same way.

children.label: All the chapters, in order
children.desc:
**Term 1 (Part I)**
- 1. Coordinates: 8 periods
- 2. Linear Polynomials: 9 periods
- 3. The World of Numbers: 10 periods
- 4. Algebraic Identities: 10 periods
- 5. Circles: 8 periods
- 6. Perimeter and Area: 8 periods
- 7. Probability: 6 periods
- 8. Sequences and Progressions: 7 periods

**Term 2 (Part II)**
- 9. Propositions and Converses: 4 periods
- 10. Combining Data: 6 periods
- 11. Algorithms: 5 periods
- 12. Quadrilaterals: 6 periods
- 13. Linear Equations in Two Variables: 7 periods
- 14. Surface Area and Volume: 7 periods

The lesson plans add up to **66 periods** in Term 1 and **35** in Term 2.

children.label: How the chapters connect across the year
children.desc:
Term 2 keeps reaching back into Term 1:
- **Chapter 12** (quadrilaterals) uses Chapter 5's triangle facts and Chapter 9's converses.
- **Chapter 13** (two variables, one line) joins Chapter 1's points with Chapter 2's 'start plus jump', which also came back in Chapter 8's APs.
- **Chapter 14** (surface area and volume) is Chapter 6 in three dimensions: fence or floor becomes wrapping or filling.
- **Chapter 10** (combining data) uses Chapter 7's fractions and percentages on real data.
- **Chapter 11** (algorithms) finds the greatest common divisor, which Chapter 3 used to simplify fractions.

So a gap in Term 1 often shows up in Term 2. The *Needs first* line in each chapter below says where to look.

topics.label: Term 1: Part I, Chapters 1 to 8
topics.desc:
Eight chapters, about **66 periods**. Numbers, algebra and the first geometry of the year.

Open the Term 1 start page for the thread through these chapters and pacing notes.

children.label: 1. Coordinates
children.desc:
**The one idea:** Two numbers pin down any spot: go across first, then up.

**Needs first:** Negative numbers and squaring. The roadmap's *Start here* covers both.

31 steps (20 on the core path), and a 8-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 2. Linear Polynomials
children.desc:
**The one idea:** A start, plus the same jump every time.

**Needs first:** Chapter 1, for plotting points.

36 steps (25 on the core path), and a 9-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 3. The World of Numbers
children.desc:
**The one idea:** A family of numbers that keeps growing, because each kind could not do a job the next one can.

**Needs first:** Fractions. The roadmap fixes them first.

44 steps (30 on the core path), and a 10-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 4. Algebraic Identities
children.desc:
**The one idea:** An identity is a picture of an area: a square or rectangle cut into pieces.

**Needs first:** Chapter 2's words of algebra (terms and coefficients). Like terms and brackets are fixed inside the chapter.

45 steps (33 on the core path), and a 10-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 5. Circles
children.desc:
**The one idea:** Every radius is the same length, which gives an isosceles triangle and a hidden right triangle.

**Needs first:** Triangle angles and Pythagoras. Chapter 1's distance formula helps.

35 steps (23 on the core path), and a 8-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 6. Perimeter and Area
children.desc:
**The one idea:** Fence or floor? Every area formula is a cut-and-rearrange picture.

**Needs first:** Chapter 3 (π is irrational) and Chapter 5 (arcs and sectors). Chapter 4's area pictures help.

33 steps (23 on the core path), and a 8-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 7. Probability
children.desc:
**The one idea:** Probability is the ways you want divided by all the ways.

**Needs first:** Fractions only. This chapter can be done early.

29 steps (20 on the core path), and a 6-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 8. Sequences and Progressions
children.desc:
**The one idea:** Do the same thing every time: add the same number for an AP, multiply by the same number for a GP.

**Needs first:** Chapter 2: an AP is a start plus the same jump.

33 steps (22 on the core path), and a 7-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

topics.label: Term 2: Part II, Chapters 9 to 14
topics.desc:
6 chapters, about **35 periods**. Reasoning, data, algorithms, more geometry, and solids.

Open the Term 2 start page for the thread through these chapters and pacing notes.

children.label: 9. Propositions and Converses
children.desc:
**The one idea:** An 'if ... then' statement only works one way: turn it round and check again. One counterexample is enough to show a statement is false.

**Needs first:** Multiples, factors and square numbers. The roadmap's *Start here* covers them.

27 steps (18 on the core path), and a 4-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 10. Combining Data
children.desc:
**The one idea:** An average has to remember how many: when groups combine, bigger groups count for more.

**Needs first:** Averages, percentages and ratios.

26 steps (18 on the core path), and a 6-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 11. Algorithms
children.desc:
**The one idea:** An algorithm is a recipe so exact that nobody has to think while following it, and a smarter recipe does less work.

**Needs first:** Divisors and remainders.

24 steps (14 on the core path), and a 5-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 12. Quadrilaterals
children.desc:
**The one idea:** Cut a quadrilateral into triangles, and the triangle facts you know do the work.

**Needs first:** Chapter 9 (converses) and Chapter 5 (triangle angles and congruence).

26 steps (16 on the core path), and a 6-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 13. Linear Equations in Two Variables
children.desc:
**The one idea:** Every solution is a point, one equation is a line, and two equations meet where their lines cross.

**Needs first:** Chapter 1 (plotting points) and Chapter 2 (start plus jump).

27 steps (20 on the core path), and a 7-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

children.label: 14. Surface Area and Volume
children.desc:
**The one idea:** Wrapping or filling? Surface area is the paper to wrap a solid, volume is the water to fill it.

**Needs first:** Chapter 6 (circle formulas) and Pythagoras.

27 steps (19 on the core path), and a 7-period lesson plan for teachers.

Start with the chapter's *Check yourself*: two minutes, and it tells you which small skills to fix first.

topics.label: For teachers and parents
topics.desc: **For the adults helping.** Students can skip this milestone.

children.label: Pacing the year
children.desc:
- **Term 1:** 66 periods of lesson plans across 8 chapters.
- **Term 2:** 35 periods across 6 chapters.

Each plan leaves room for revision and tests. Two suggestions for a class that is losing confidence:
- **Chapter 7** (Probability) needs only fractions and is the gentlest chapter in Term 1. Teaching it early, after Chapter 2 or 3, gives an early win.
- **Chapter 9** (Propositions) has almost no arithmetic. It is a good fresh start for Term 2, and it makes Chapter 12 easier.

children.label: Revision before each term's exams
children.desc:
Every chapter ends with a **5-minute exit ticket**: five short questions on its main ideas, with answers. Together they make a quick revision quiz for the term.

- Give each exit ticket without warning. A wrong answer names the chapter to revisit.
- For students who are struggling, go back further: that chapter's *Check yourself*.

children.label: Starting with a class that is behind
children.desc:
- Run the *Check yourself* of the **current** chapter with the whole class.
- Group students by the step each one needs, and give each group that step.
- Come back together for the chapter's first core milestone.

Two minutes of checking saves a lot of teaching that doesn't land.
